8 off the last over and 3 wickets. Keemo Paul with a fifer. An over-rate penalty for West Indies. Just 4 outside the ring. Won't matter much. 35 needed off the last over.
Shamar Joseph [2.0-0-37-0] is back into the attack
Shamar Joseph to Arshdeep Singh, FOUR, length delivery and following Arshdeep Singh outside the leg-stump, he throws the bat on that and it flies off a thick outside-edge over short third man
Shamar Joseph to Arshdeep Singh, wide, Shamar Joseph is really struggling. It's a slower-ball and wide of the tramline on the off-side, Arshdeep Singh backs away well outside the leg-stump, leaves it
Shamar Joseph to Arshdeep Singh, no run, slower-ball off-cutter and dug in short into the pitch, Arshdeep Singh comes down the track and throws the bat on that, pulls and misses

Shamar Joseph to Arshdeep Singh, no run, Arshdeep Singh is down. He is hit on the arm. Good pacy short delivery and it thuds into the left bicep of Arshdeep Singh as he backs away to pull this outside the leg-stump. The physio is out there. A break in play. Shai Hope and Keemo are all smiles meanwhile with a chat
Arshdeep Singh stretches his left arm and the on-air comms feel that it would be better if he walks off. They feel India need his services for the last ODI with the ball.

Shamar Joseph to Arshdeep Singh, 5 wides, dug in short and following Arshdeep Singh well outside the leg-stump, he pulls and misses. Shai Hope doesn't even bother to dive. Allows it to go away for wides

Arshdeep Singh is in pain and is on his haunches. Nitin Menon is having a chat. Maybe he is telling him if he can't carry on, he can walk off. Shreyas is up on the dugout and looks to be calling him in. The physio is out there. Arshdeep is in some pain. He can't continue and he is walking off. That's the end of the game. All smiles in the West Indies camp as Keemo is the man at the centre of attraction.

Keemo Paul (2/2): [On whether the must-win match added extra pressure] Well I wouldn't say extra pressure, but the guys were definitely more pumped, more hyped, much more passionate and we got the job done. So hopefully that works for us next game also. [On Motie's contribution as a spinner and his wickets against two set left-handers] Yes, I think Motie came in when there was two set batters, two left-handers and he bowled excellently. So kudos to Motie. It wasn't a tough situation but he did really, really well. [On the team's development and confidence heading into the next game] Look, I think we are a pretty confident bunch. I think all the guys, we back our skills and we feel we could beat any team on our day. So it's just about staying calm and believing in ourselves and I think we're doing that really well.

Shreyas Iyer | India Captain (1/2): [On India's performance and where they fell short in the chase] It all started with bowling. I think we didn't execute our line lengths well and see at the end of the day chasing 250 you have to go in a certain pattern when you're coming and chasing. So I like the approach when we were chasing but we were unfortunate we couldn't execute our plans in bowling and that's where we fell a bit short. [On whether Abhishek Sharma being off strike early affected India's start] Not really, we were still going 12 an over at that point of time. It's just that they executed their plan and there was a bit too off from the wicket as well. The ball was kicking a bit and they used the field pretty well. So credit where it's due and their execution was spot on.

Shreyas Iyer (2/2): [On the pitch slowing down and offering extra bounce during the middle overs] Yeah, it was holding a bit and there were some more bounces as well. But yeah, knowing that I feel the bowlers, they realized it. They are bowlers and the way they bowled according to the field, that's what was important, especially in those middle overs. Even though the momentum shifted towards us, in between still the ability to bounce back was top notch and I'm sure the fifth one would be an interesting one. [On the surface after it was used and India's approach going into the next game] Well, obviously, getting 220, especially when we were chasing and then scoring 250, you can see the approach and attitude of every individual. So the approach is going to be same and I feel going forward we don't have to think much about, our bowling. But it's all about execution and having that fresh mindset where you come on that given day and see do it, then you seize the moment.

Shai Hope (2/2): [On the decision to give Gudakesh Motie only two overs despite his two wickets] Well just, here in India, it's always tough to give bowlers three in a row, especially on conditions maybe say, yes, give him another one. But sometimes you just have to make a decision and back it. Just one of those things that happened today. [On West Indies' ability to defend totals in slightly drier conditions] Yeah, for sure. Conditions were a little bit more similar for both sides. I just felt as though (with) the dew around, it's always going to be a part of the sphere when they chase it. Again, a really good cricket game. They played good cricket in all phases as well. So you got to give them credit. But we did well to give ourselves a chance to win the series in Bangalore.

What a response from West Indies! They have bounced back in style, levelling the series 2-2 and ensuring that everything will be decided in the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday. We couldn’t have asked for a better finish to this series. For the second game in a row, the side batting first has prevailed, with less dew and variable bounce making the chase increasingly challenging. Shai Hope laid the foundation with a brilliant century, adding to the incredible run of hundreds we have witnessed on this tour, before Keemo Paul turned the game on its head with a sensational five-wicket haul, cleverly varying his pace to keep the Indian batters guessing. But there’s still one final chapter to be written, and Saturday’s decider promises to be a cracker. We will be here nice and early to bring you all the updates. For now, it’s time to wrap things up. Goodbye, good night, and take care!
